Two comments. First is that what's going on is slimy as fuck.

Secondly, this is another example of how Valve is complicit in steering gaming into a pretty shady area that is bad for consumers and gaming in general. Folks shouldn't forget that Valve attempted to start charging for mods as well, and the CSGO marketplace is pretty much just that...and it's devolved into a billion-dollar shit-show where kids are being encouraged to (illegally) gamble. I'm only pointing this out because Valve gets it's own kind of "pussy-pass" on almost everything--especially here on Voat where the Linux crowd refuses to acknowledge their proclivity for shenanigans (because they desperately want gaming on Linux to be a thing). Valve is a virtual monopoly and it has and continues to implement and impose a shit-ton of anti-gamer, anti-consumer stuff. It's difficult to avoid buying from them but don't defend them just because they are currently pushing Linux or have a good sale. They're shady as fuck and Gabe Newell is a big cry-baby who can't get enough money or food and pitches a fit when anybody dares compete with him.

I think that when Valve first made the decision to have a community market they saw it as a way for themselves to fund continued development on these games. I think that initially they had no idea what they had wrought. But it became obvious really quickly what was happening and what was going to happen. Money ruins everything and it's ruined competitive gaming on platforms like CS:GO - Make a team full of hackers, throw matches and bet on the other team on gambling sites, make insane amounts of money.

As for paid mods, the skins in CS:GO are basically paid mods. A lot of them are user submitted and some artists in the community make some money and people are cool with that. The difference though, is that Valve takes them over and maintains them. The paid mod idea was horrible from a widespread maintenance stand point. If the game's dev team doesn't become responsible for making sure they work with each new version then you're at the mercy of the mod's original author who may not even be alive anymore. It's a terrible system.

you're a bit more generous than I am with Valve. They're an incredibly wealthy company that operates as a virtual monopoly in the PC gaming space. They know what they're doing when they make moves--and their previous attempts at monetizing mods was absolutely anti-gamer and ran contrary to the entire tradition of PC gaming. It was a greedy money-grab and they got called out on it. The CS:GO stuff isn't much different other than the fact that they weren't called out on it and now they've helped create a major scandal that will almost certainly result in governments getting involved in PC gaming and regulating shit. On top of that, they've pioneered onerous DRM schemes, mainstreamed the sale of bug-ridden games barely in alpha stages as "early access" and gone to incredible lengths to spread FUD about Microsoft/Windows solely because they don't want any competition. It's worth pointing this out because Steam and especially Gabe are pretty much worshiped by the broader gaming community and--generally speaking--the evade criticism even when it's well deserved. I'm one of the very first people to ever open a Steam account and I am loving my Steam Link (and Steam Controller to a certain degree). I give them credit when they deserve it, but the gaming community needs to stop with the GabeN memes and instead start holding Valve accountable for it's anti-consumer/anti-gamer/pro-monopoly bullshit. This CS:GO gambling shit--which Valve helped spawn--is going to result in government regulation of gaming...and that ain't good for any of us.
